prompt:
Scene:
A square color magazine advertisement page in the style of 1962 American futurist home print ads. Full product-hero layout: appliance centered on a gradient studio backdrop, top banner area, bottom tagline area. Halftone grain, slight CMYK offset on edges, matte coated-paper feel.

Subject:
An imaginary atomic-age countertop food-pill dispenser: a chrome torpedo-shaped tabletop unit with two bulbous glass hoppers on top filled with colorful round pills (cadmium red, bright yellow, turquoise, powder pink). A chrome chute at the front has just deposited four assorted pills onto a small ivory porcelain plate. A cadmium-red dial selector is on the side. A stylized mid-century father figure in an ivory shirt and thin black tie smiles at the viewer while holding the plate, clearly pleased that dinner is ready. Backdrop is a soft turquoise-to-powder-pink gradient.

Important details:
Strict atomic-age palette: ivory, turquoise, cadmium red, bright yellow, powder pink, chrome. The dispenser must feel like 1962 imagined-future kitchen tech: chrome torpedo body, glass hoppers, analog dial. Pills look like colorful candy, not medicine capsules. Illustration style is halftone print ad, not photo. Father is a stylized cartoon figure with a magazine-ad smile.

Use case:
Atomic Appliance Studies single study 4 of 5, independent product ad mockup.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, no pharmacy bottles, no medical imagery, no LCD display, no photoreal skin, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio.
